title: Five positive matchings for C_3 □ C_4: a finite counterexample to Conjecture 4.7 of arXiv:2502.02826
exact_endpoint: TorusPMD.refutes_conjecture_4_7 : ¬ ∀ m n, 3 ≤ m → 3 ≤ n → Even (m + n) ∨ (m, n) = (3, 4) ∨ (m, n) = (3, 6) ∨ (m, n) = (5, 6) → pmd (torus m n) = 6, with pmd the literal minimum positive matching decomposition number on the Cartesian product of cycles
scope: Farrokhi D. G. and Yazdan Pour, arXiv:2502.02826v1, Conjecture 4.7 (pmd(C_m □ C_n) = 6 for m + n even or (m, n) in {(3,4), (3,6), (5,6)}). False: C_3 □ C_4 has a five-part positive matching decomposition, and pmd(C_3 □ C_4) = 5 exactly; supporting certificates show pmd = 5 also at (3,5), (3,6) and (3,7).
fidelity_review: pmd-review-r1/REVIEW.md (A-C PASS including Lean definition fidelity and strict compile; D-E QUALIFIED_PASS)
dependency_closure_audited: local declarations audited (axioms and metadata); upstream Mathlib oleans trusted
substantive_reason: It refutes a 2025 exact-value conjecture at a case the authors explicitly excluded from their own theorem and conjectured to be 6. The exact value is 5, by an explicit certificate and a short regular-graph lower bound; the same value at (3,5), (3,6) and (3,7) shows the conjectured value fails more broadly in the m = 3 family. Significance is modest: a finite-search counterexample without a general torus formula.
